newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins set further records, track Bradies.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins set further records, track Bradies.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds set new records tracking sentiment in other emerging markets, dealers said on Wednesday, forecasting the trend would last through the week on expectations of U.S. data seen as positive.
Dealers forecast further rise of MinFins at least until Friday when the U.S. June Producer Price Index is due. Economists forecast PPI would be unchanged.
"PPI figures are expected to be good for the market, so it is bulls who are ruling the market," Kovzharov said.
One dealer said Treasuries, which often lead MinFins, had pushed the market up for the day.
"The rise was due to the global upward trend of emerging markets, buoyed by the move in U.S. Treasury securities," the dealer said.
MinFins set records was last Wednesday when U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) left interest rates unchanged at a regular meeting.

"MinFins setting records daily is already an ordinary thing," Moscow Bussiness World dealer Sergei Kovzharov said. "Buying has started in the morning and the trend is supported in London and New York."
He added MinFins had additional support from the rise of Vnesh loans.
